title: A Genome-Scale TF-DNA Interaction Network of Transcriptional Regulation of Arabidopsis Primary and Specialized Metabolism
authors: Michelle Tang; Baohua Li; Xue Zhou; Tayah Bolt; Jia Jie Li; Neiman Cruz; Allison Gaudinier; Richard Ngo; Caitlin Clark-Wiest; Daniel J. Kliebenstein; Siobhan M. Brady
one_liner_zh: 该文构建拟南芥代谢基因的基因组规模TF-DNA互作网络，虽聚焦TF-DNA结合位点映射，但以实验方法为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作资源，对本课题有参考价值但深度不足。
abstract: In single-celled microbes, transcriptional regulation by single transcription factors is sufficient to shift primary metabolism. Corresponding genome-level transcriptional regulatory maps of metabolism reveal the underlying design principles responsible for these shifts as a model in which master regulators largely coordinate specific metabolic pathways. Relative to individual microbes, plant metabolism is more complex. Primary and specialized metabolism occur within innumerable cell types, and their reactions shift depending on internal and external cues. Given the importance of plants and their metabolites in providing humanity with food, fiber and medicine, we set out to develop a genome-scale transcriptional regulatory map of Arabidopsis metabolic genes. A comprehensive set of protein-DNA interactions between Arabidopsis thaliana transcription factors and promoters of primary metabolism and specialized metabolism were mapped. To demonstrate the utility of this resource, we identified and functionally validated regulators of the TCA cycle. The resulting network suggests that plant metabolic design principles are distinct from that of microbes. Instead, metabolism appears to be transcriptionally coordinated via developmental- and stress-conditional processes that can coordinate across primary and specialized metabolism. These data represent the most comprehensive resource of interactions between TFs and metabolic genes in plants.
abstract_zh: 在单细胞微生物中，单一转录因子（transcription factor）的调控足以改变初级代谢。相应的基因组层面代谢转录调控图谱揭示了这些转变背后的设计原理，表现为主调控因子主要协调特定代谢途径的模型。相较于单个微生物，植物代谢更为复杂。初级代谢和特化代谢发生在无数细胞类型中，其反应随内外信号而变化。鉴于植物及其代谢物在提供人类食物、纤维和药物方面的重要性，我们着手构建拟南芥代谢基因的基因组规模转录调控图谱。我们绘制了拟南芥（Arabidopsis thaliana）转录因子与初级代谢及特化代谢启动子之间全面的蛋白质-DNA相互作用图谱。为展示该资源的实用性，我们鉴定并功能验证了三羧酸循环（TCA cycle）的调控因子。所得网络表明，植物的代谢设计原理与微生物不同。相反，代谢似乎通过发育和胁迫条件性过程进行转录协调，这些过程可跨越初级代谢和特化代谢进行协调。这些数据代表了植物中转录因子与代谢基因相互作用最全面的资源。
